articles.title: The Minecraft Locator Bar across versions: a command reference that explains what each control actually changes
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I built and run Locator Lab, an independent site about the Minecraft Locator Bar. It isn't an official Minecraft product and isn't affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft. The Locator Bar is t…
articles.body: Disclosure: I built and run Locator Lab , an independent site about the Minecraft Locator Bar. It isn't an official Minecraft product and isn't affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft. The Locator Bar is the multiplayer HUD strip that points toward other players with coloured markers. It sits in the experience bar area. It's a small feature with an unusually messy command history: two editions, three rule names and a colour system with its own priority order. Most "the command doesn't work" reports come down to running a correct command on the wrong version. This is the reference I wish I'd had when I started keeping notes on it. It starts with a timeline, then gives a mental model with three layers, and ends with the server-side traps.

articles.title: Building a Chrome Extension That Compares UI Elements Across Pages
articles.excerpt: Chrome DevTools offers powerful capabilities for inspecting web interfaces. But when reviewing visual consistency across a product, I often find that the challenge isn't inspecting one element. It's c…
articles.body: Chrome DevTools offers powerful capabilities for inspecting web interfaces. But when reviewing visual consistency across a product, I often find that the challenge isn't inspecting one element. It's comparing several elements across different screens. Consider a checkout flow with buttons appearing on different pages. You might want to check whether their typography, padding, colors, and borders are consistent. Individually inspecting each button and manually comparing its CSS properties becomes repetitive. I wanted a lightweight tool that could capture those properties, preserve them across navigation, and display the differences in one place. That idea became Visqora , a free Chrome extension built with React, TypeScript, WXT, and Manifest V3.

articles.title: Claim guest responses by transferring control of a record, not matching a name
articles.excerpt: Someone answers an event invitation without logging in and later wants to change the response. Using their name as proof of identity cannot distinguish namesakes or a different person logging in on a…
articles.body: Someone answers an event invitation without logging in and later wants to change the response. Using their name as proof of identity cannot distinguish namesakes or a different person logging in on a shared device. SquadNote issues a token controlling one response instead of creating a placeholder user row. Later login does not automatically match names: the person reviews the target responses and explicitly claims them for the account. A response token grants control of a record; identifying a person requires separate evidence. This investigation read the design, migration, API, and device-storage code at circle-hub commit 9aec489 , then reran related tests on September 11, 2026.

articles.title: Case Study: Making My Portfolio Loud (Without Making It Slow)
articles.excerpt: My portfolio worked fine. That was the problem. It was a tidy neubrutalist site: yellow, cyan and green cards, thick black borders, hard drop shadows, a dark-mode toggle. And it did its job: it helped…
articles.body: My portfolio worked fine. That was the problem. It was a tidy neubrutalist site: yellow, cyan and green cards, thick black borders, hard drop shadows, a dark-mode toggle. And it did its job: it helped me land Oatopia , Rev6 and Digital Trek (Rodentia Pest Products) as clients. But it looked like a lot of other neubrutalist portfolios, and a UX audit I'd been working through kept pointing out the same thing. It was clean and it was forgettable. So I tried something I'd normally talk myself out of. I went maximalist. Kinetic type, colours that clash, stickers you can throw around, marquees that react to your scroll. Internally I called it the loud redesign . This post covers what I built, the rules that kept it usable, and the bugs that caught me out.

articles.title: Why a score's printed beat and playback BPM need separate units
articles.excerpt: A printed tempo mark can say eighth note = 120, while a playback timeline measures speed in quarter notes per minute. Treating both numbers as the same BPM would double the intended playback rate. Pia…
articles.body: A printed tempo mark can say eighth note = 120, while a playback timeline measures speed in quarter notes per minute. Treating both numbers as the same BPM would double the intended playback rate. Pianory keeps the score's beat unit for display and converts to a canonical quarter-note rate for timeline math. In tempo.ts , a TempoMark stores the printed unit, whether it is dotted, the printed per-minute value, and quarterBpm . beatQuarters maps half, quarter and eighth notes to 2, 1 and 0.5 quarter notes respectively, then multiplies by 1.5 for one dot. So an eighth-note mark at 120 beats per minute becomes 60 quarter notes per minute. The label function reverses that conversion for the player UI, leaving the score's printed ♪ = 120 intact.

articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.

articles.title: Halley's Comet dazzles from afar in spectacular astrophoto of Orionid meteor shower
articles.excerpt: This incredible composite image of Orionid meteors was captured as Earth passed through the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet.
articles.body: Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.
